FACTOR IO / KUBERNETES · INFRASTRUCTURE · ENTERPRISE AI

Kubernetes, infrastructure, and the AI that runs on it.

Factor IO builds the platform layer that any enterprise workload can run on. AI is the workload at the front of the queue right now, and it is our specialisation — model serving, knowledge systems, and the governance that decides what AI is allowed to do. The platform underneath is what makes it survivable.

Talk about your projectWork with us as a partner

01 / Focus

The platform is general. The specialisation is not.

Kubernetes and the infrastructure under it are built to carry whatever the business needs to run — applications, data, batch work, and the workload nobody has chosen yet. That generality is the point: a platform built around one workload has to be rebuilt when the next one arrives. What we go deep on today is AI, because AI is what is arriving. Both statements matter and they are not the same claim. The platform is where the durability is. AI is where the specialisation is.

02 / Production

Plan for the day people start relying on it.

We work through these questions during design. Then we test against agreed requirements and prepare your team to operate the system. If you already have a pilot, we can assess what it needs before it goes into production.

  1. ?

    Who can access the data?

    Access follows the roles and approvals your organisation already uses. It gets settled during design, not after the system is live.

  2. ?

    How will you check the answers?

    Results are tested against requirements you agreed, so a reviewer can check the work rather than having to trust it.

  3. ?

    What happens when something fails?

    Failure handling is part of the design: what stops, what is retried, and who gets told about it.

  4. ?

    Who will look after the system?

    Your team. We prepare them to operate it, and the procedures are written down before handover.

03 / Services

The platform first, then what runs on it.

Most engagements start with the infrastructure and grow into the workloads it carries. Each of these can stand on its own or be one stage of the same delivery.

  1. 01

    Kubernetes and infrastructure

    The platform your applications need, including Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure. It is designed to carry whatever the business runs on it rather than one workload in particular. Capacity, recovery, upgrades and day-to-day ownership are part of the design.

  2. 02

    Enterprise AI

    Tell us what you want AI to do for the business. We help define the scope, choose an approach and build it into your existing environment.

  3. 03

    Knowledge systems

    Make your organisation's information useful to AI: which sources to trust, who can access them, and how to keep them current.

  4. 04

    AI governance

    Decide what AI may do on its own and when a person needs to approve the next step. We design the controls around those decisions, and how they will be tested.

04 / Engagement routes

Two ways to bring us in.

The technical work is the same. What changes is who is sitting in front of the customer.

  • For your business

    Engage us to assess an existing system, design a new solution or carry a project through delivery. We agree the scope, responsibilities and acceptance criteria with you before implementation begins.

    Who holds the customer relationshipYou hold it, and we are accountable to you for the technical scope we agreed.

  • For technology partners

    Bring us into an opportunity that needs senior architecture or delivery expertise. We work alongside vendors, distributors and systems integrators, supporting customer discovery, solution design, technical validation and implementation.

    Who holds the customer relationshipYour team holds it, and we take responsibility for the agreed technical work.

06 / Process

Start with the problem you need to solve.

Four stages, agreed with you before anything gets built.

  1. 01

    Understand the requirement

    Review your goals, existing systems and constraints. Identify what needs attention first.

  2. 02

    Agree the design

    Set the scope, architecture and acceptance criteria so you know what will be delivered.

  3. 03

    Build and test

    Implement the agreed solution. Use a focused pilot where an assumption needs testing before wider deployment.

  4. 04

    Deploy and hand over

    Prepare the operating procedures and work through them with your team. Agree any ongoing support separately.
